query: An equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy has a simple solid-solution structure and favorable plasticity and machinability but relatively low hardness and strength, while its microstructure and deformation behavior remain insufficiently understood. Under hardness testing and mechanical loading of this starting state, what single intervention could overcome the strength and hardness limitation while retaining its favorable mechanical characteristics? State the proposed intervention, its mechanism, the predicted measurable change relative to the unmodified alloy, its applicable processing and test conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a microstructural and mechanical experiment that could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy can be strengthened by introducing a minor amount of boron, which induces the precipitation of hexagonal close-packed borides at the grain boundaries, thereby enhancing grain boundary cohesion and improving work hardenability and ductility.
generation.material_initial_state: equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy with a simple solid-solution structure
generation.intervention: addition of a minor amount of boron (e.g., 0.1 at.%)
generation.conditions: processing and testing conditions similar to those used for the HfMoNbTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloy
generation.structural_mediator: precipitation of hexagonal close-packed borides at grain boundaries
generation.mechanism: enhanced grain boundary cohesion and improved work hardenability and ductility due to boride precipitation
generation.predicted_outcome: improved strength and hardness while retaining favorable mechanical characteristics
generation.boundary: limits of boron addition and processing conditions
generation.uncertainty: effects of boron addition on microstructure and properties, optimal boron content and processing conditions

falsification_experiment.design: microstructural and mechanical characterization of CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy with and without boron addition
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: if no significant improvement in strength and hardness is observed with boron addition, the hypothesis is falsified

Own digest: Microstructure and Mechanical Properties of Intergranular Boride Precipitation-Toughened HfMoNbTaTiZr Refractory High-Entropy Alloy

Abstract: AbstractTo develop strong refractory high-entropy alloys for use at elevated temperatures as well as to overcome grain-boundary brittleness, an equimolar HfMoNbTaTiZr alloy was prepared, and a minor amount of boron (0.1 at.%) was added into the alloy. The microstructures of the alloys were characterized, and their macro-to-microscale mechanical properties were measured. The microstructural observations indicated that the matrices of both the alloys were composed of a body-centered cubic solid-solution structure, and the added boron induced the precipitation of hexagonal close-packed borides (most likely the (Hf, Zr)B2) at the grain boundaries.
